paper text.text:
Suppose $G$ has a torus embedding and restrict it to $K$.
The connected interior of $B$ lies in one face $F$, whose
boundary contains all four attachments. For each of the
three pairs $(n_c,n_d)$, the rotations of $K$ and their
boundary attachment sequences are given in~\supp{R4}.
Let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular neighborhood of $K$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, if $\mathcal N$ has
genus one, every complementary region is a disk.
If it has genus zero, the complementary regions are disks
together with exactly one annulus or one torus with an
open disk removed. For a disk face, let $H_0$ consist of
the attachments and the edges joining consecutive
attachments on its boundary, as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}.

Suppose the retained graph has a torus embedding. Since $B$ joins $c,d$, a genus-one regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ would give $B$ a planar two-edge completion by Lemma~\ref{r2:cellular-center}. Its regular neighborhood therefore has genus zero. In this case each boundary walk contains at most two distinct attachment labels~\supp{R4}. Both $B$ and the star at $v$ have three attachments, so each requires a region with at least two boundary components. By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} they lie in the same annulus. Since together they meet all four attachments, the boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$~\supp{R4}.

Suppose a shortening in (i) or (ii) of
Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration} is
possible. It keeps the interior connected
and preserves all three attachments,
giving a proper minor of $G$.
Take a torus embedding of this minor.
The subgraph $\Psi_2$ and every bridge's attachments are unchanged.
If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ has genus zero, no boundary
walk contains three attachments or both $c,d$~\supp{R4}. The shortened
bridge therefore cannot lie in a disk or a torus with one open disk
removed, since each has only one boundary walk. Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}
then forces an annulus, containing every bridge with three attachments
and $cd$ if present. Thus the disk and annulus tests apply.
For a disk containing the shortened bridge, take $H=C_F$, the boundary
cycle in its planar test graph. For an annulus, the additions still meet
all four vertices, so its boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$.
Take $H$ to consist of the two added
edges of the annulus test together
with $cd$ or another bridge.
The edge $cd$ joins the two added
edges, and any bridge with three
attachments meets both. Thus $H$
is connected, contains all four
attachment appearances, and avoids
the interior of the shortened bridge. Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration}
therefore restores $B$ in the planar
test graph, keeping the other edges
and their attachment appearances fixed.
Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}
or Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}
then gives a torus embedding of $G$,
a contradiction.

what: Every rotation system of Psi_2 with n_c vertices of neighbourhood {a,b,c} (p, q, and p3 when n_c = 3) and n_d of neighbourhood {a,b,d} (r, z, and r3 when n_d = 3), for (n_c, n_d) = (2, 2), (3, 2) and (3, 3). Attachments a, b, c, d; twins omitted.
how to read: For each graph: 'cyclic orders' lists, for every vertex, all cyclic orders of its neighbours, each starting with its alphabetically first neighbour (the other neighbours follow in every possible order, in lexicographic order). Rotation system number i (counting from 0) takes at each vertex the cyclic order whose position is the corresponding digit of i, written in the mixed radix given by the numbers of cyclic orders in the order of 'vertices', the last vertex varying fastest (the order of Python's itertools.product). Facial walks are traced by the rule used throughout the supplement: after the dart u->v comes v->w, where w follows u in the cyclic order at v. The genus is (2 - V + E - F)/2. The attachment sequence of a facial walk lists the attachments it passes through, in walk order, one entry per passage; it is written from its lexicographically least cyclic shift, keeping the direction of the walk, and the faces of a row are sorted. Since many rotation systems give the same row, the distinct rows are listed once under 'distinct rows' and 'rows' gives, for every rotation system in order, the position of its row in that list. 'Up to cyclic shift and reversal' in the claims means the least sequence among all cyclic shifts of the sequence and of its reverse.

claims.statement: (n_c, n_d) = (2, 2): the genus-one attachment sequences meeting all four attachments, up to cyclic shift and reversal, with H obtained by joining consecutive attachments; each H is a cycle, a triangle with a pendant edge or a three-edge star, and the sequence is a facial walk of H.

Only (n_c, n_d) = (2, 2) has planar rotations. Their boundary attachment sequences are ab, ab, ac, bc, ad, bd. No single walk contains all four attachments, and both annular pairs ac | bd and ad | bc occur.
For (2, 2) in genus one, the sequences of length four or five give graphs H containing ac, bd or ad, bc; the remaining sequences give the tests B+ab+ac+ad and B+ab+bc+bd, and each occurs.

When a closed regular neighbourhood of Psi_2 has genus zero, its boundary attachment sequences are ab, ab, ac, bc, ad, bd. No single boundary walk contains three attachments or both c and d, and the pairs of walks together containing c and d are ac | bd, ad | bc, ac | ad, bc | bd.

There are 576 rotations of Psi_2; 80 of genus one have a facial walk containing both c and d, and in every face of these rotations containing at least three attachment labels, no two labels alternate as u, v, u, v.

(n_c, n_d) = (3, 2): the genus-one attachment sequences meeting all four attachments, up to cyclic shift and reversal, with H obtained by joining consecutive attachments; each H is a cycle, a triangle with a pendant edge or a three-edge star, and the sequence is a facial walk of H.
For (3, 2), the sequences abcad and abdbc are facial walks of the triangle abc with pendant edge ad or bd, giving B+ab+ac+bc+ad and B+ab+ac+bc+bd; acbd gives B+ac+bc+bd+ad.

(n_c, n_d) = (3, 3): the genus-one attachment sequences meeting all four attachments, up to cyclic shift and reversal, with H obtained by joining consecutive attachments; each H is a cycle, a triangle with a pendant edge or a three-edge star, and the sequence is a facial walk of H.
